review_protocol: two independent reviewers; disagreement requires third-reviewer arbitration

items.question: Does the repository contain a reachable consumer that makes the retained event list security-relevant?
Is there a concrete allocator/deallocator mismatch rather than a same-flag no-op cleanup path?
Does the borrowed pointer reach a concrete post-lifetime dereference under the declared API contract?
Does the callback contract consume or dereference the escaped pointer after lifetime end?
Is the ownership-transfer obligation concrete and field-sensitive on every relevant exit?
Does the flat allocation contain an owned child resource whose cleanup is actually missing?
Is the structured sink the post-unlock access rather than the access inside the critical section?
Is concurrent external invocation part of an answer-free project-level API threat contract?
Is the required caller/concurrency contract present without assuming truth-specific deployment behavior?
